facts.t: India's parliamentary privileges have never been codified
facts.d: Articles 105(3) and 194(3) originally referred to the privileges of the House of Commons. Parliament was expected to define its own — seventy-five years later it still has not, so their scope is settled case by case.

facts.t: A legislature once tried to imprison High Court judges
facts.d: In the Keshav Singh case of 1964 the UP Assembly ordered the arrest of two Allahabad High Court judges who had granted him bail. The resulting Presidential Reference established that privileges are not absolute and remain subject to judicial review.

facts.t: Only the word may be expunged, not the paragraph
facts.d: Rule 380 lets the Speaker strike unparliamentary expressions from the record. The power extends to the offending word itself — not to whole sentences or passages of a member's speech.

bank.q: Sita Soren (2024) was decided by a bench of:
bank.e: A seven-judge bench, unanimously overruling P. V. Narasimha Rao (1998).

bank.q: With reference to the two-fold test in Sita Soren, consider the following:
s: The act must relate to the collective functioning of the House.
It must bear a functional relationship to the legislator's duty.
Bribery satisfies the first limb but fails the second.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 state the test. Bribery fails both limbs, not merely the second.

bank.q: Match List I (case) with List II (holding on privilege):
pairs: 1. Privileges are not absolute and are subject to judicial review
3. Acting in a private capacity does not attract Article 194
4. Punishment does not extend to future disqualification
bank.e: The Searchlight case on the priority of privilege over free speech, Keshav Singh on reviewability, Raja Ram Pal on the limits of punishment, and Jatish Chandra Ghosh on private capacity.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT correct about breach of privilege and contempt?
o: A breach of privilege is also contempt of the House
Every contempt of the House is necessarily a breach of privilege
Privileges attach to the House collectively, to committees and to members
Privileges exist to prevent interference with essential functions
bank.e: The relationship runs one way only — a breach of privilege amounts to contempt, but contempt need not involve a breach of any specific privilege.

bank.as: Legislators receive differential legal treatment from ordinary citizens.
bank.rs: They form a particular class of public officials whose duties require freedom from intimidation while speaking and voting.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — the functional justification for privilege, and the reason Sita Soren refused to extend it to bribery.

bank.q: Consider the following appropriate consequences for legislator conduct:
s: Open, publicly explained dissent should attract political or party consequences.
A vote exchanged for money warrants criminal prosecution and possible disqualification.
Cross-voting should automatically be treated as corruption.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The framework expressly warns against equating cross-voting with corruption.

bank.q: All of the following are identified as problems with the present privileges regime EXCEPT:
o: Conflict with free speech and other fundamental rights
Excessive judicial interference in House proceedings
bank.e: The concern runs the other way — privileges limit judicial review, which is listed as a problem rather than judicial overreach.

bank.q: Which proposal is advanced to resolve the uncertainty around privileges?
o: A Parliamentary Privileges Commission leading to codification
Transferring privilege matters to the Supreme Court
Making all privilege decisions subject to referendum
bank.e: A dedicated commission and codification, alongside legislator training and stronger committee scrutiny.

bank.q: With reference to the proposed election-integrity framework, consider the following:
s: Time-bound investigation of alleged bribery in elections.
Whistle-blower protection for MLAs and mandatory reporting of attempted inducements.
An explicit power for the Election Commission to countermand a materially compromised poll, subject to prompt judicial review.
bank.e: All three form part of the proposed framework, along with fast-track courts and interim preservation of electronic, financial and travel records.

bank.q: In the Searchlight case the Court held that in a conflict between Article 194(3) and Article 19(1)(a):
o: The special protection of privilege prevails
The conflict must be resolved by the Speaker
Both are equally weighted and must be harmonised
bank.e: The special provision was held to prevail over the general right — a holding later qualified by Keshav Singh's insistence that privileges cannot violate fundamental rights.
